## Advanced Techniques

### Validating Clone Detection Results

After running `tree_trimmer()` and cutting your tree, you should validate the results:

```{r validation, eval=FALSE}
library(treeTrimmer)

# Run clone detection
result <- tree_trimmer(hc, tech_reps)
clone_groups <- cutree(hc, h = result$height)

# Calculate within-cluster diversity
cluster_stats <- lapply(unique(clone_groups), function(clust) {
  members <- which(clone_groups == clust)
  if (length(members) > 1) {
    # Get IBS values within this cluster
    ibs_within <- ibs_matrix[members, members]
    ibs_within[lower.tri(ibs_within, diag = TRUE)] <- NA
    
    data.frame(
      cluster = clust,
      n_members = length(members),
      mean_ibs = mean(ibs_within, na.rm = TRUE),
      min_ibs = min(ibs_within, na.rm = TRUE),
      max_ibs = max(ibs_within, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  }
}) %>% bind_rows()

# Flag suspicious clusters (low within-cluster IBS)
suspicious <- cluster_stats %>% filter(min_ibs < 0.90)

if (nrow(suspicious) > 0) {
  warning("Found ", nrow(suspicious), " clusters with low within-cluster IBS")
  print(suspicious)
}
```

### Handling Multiple Sequencing Batches

If you have technical replicates from different sequencing runs, they might have higher technical variation:

```{r batch-effects, eval=FALSE}
# Separate replicates by batch
batch1_reps <- list(
  OGM024 = c("OGM024_batch1_rep1", "OGM024_batch1_rep2"),
  OGM066 = c("OGM066_batch1_rep1", "OGM066_batch1_rep2")
)

batch2_reps <- list(
  OGM024 = c("OGM024_batch2_rep1", "OGM024_batch2_rep2"),
  OGM066 = c("OGM066_batch2_rep1", "OGM066_batch2_rep2")
)

# Run separately
result_batch1 <- tree_trimmer(hc, batch1_reps)
result_batch2 <- tree_trimmer(hc, batch2_reps)

# Use the more conservative (higher) threshold
final_height <- max(result_batch1$height, result_batch2$height)
```

### Custom Clustering Methods

By default, most users run `hclust()` with `method = "average"` (UPGMA), but you can experiment:

```{r clustering-methods, eval=FALSE}
# Try different methods
methods <- c("average", "complete", "ward.D2")

results <- lapply(methods, function(m) {
  hc <- hclust(dist_matrix, method = m)
  result <- tree_trimmer(hc, tech_reps, verbose = FALSE)
  data.frame(
    method = m,
    height = result$height,
    max_raw = result$max_raw_height
  )
}) %>% bind_rows()

print(results)

# Use the method that gives most stable results
```

### Dealing with Uneven Replication

Not all colonies have the same number of technical replicates:

```{r uneven-reps, eval=FALSE}
tech_reps <- list(
  OGM024 = c("OGM024.1", "OGM024.2", "OGM024.3"),  # 3 reps
  OGM066 = c("OGM066.1", "OGM066.2"),              # 2 reps
  OGM108 = c("OGM108.1", "OGM108.2", "OGM108.3", "OGM108.4")  # 4 reps
)

# tree_trimmer handles this automatically
result <- tree_trimmer(hc, tech_reps)

# Check if sample size affects threshold
result$group_sizes
result$group_heights

# If the group with most reps has the highest threshold,
# that's expected (more chances for technical variation)
```

## Troubleshooting

### Problem: High Variation in Technical Replicates

**Symptom:** Your technical replicates unify at very different heights.

```{r diagnose-variation, eval=FALSE}
result <- tree_trimmer(hc, tech_reps, verbose = TRUE)

# Check the group_heights
print(result$group_heights)

# If one group is much higher than others:
#   OGM024: 0.012
#   OGM066: 0.014
#   OGM108: 0.089  # << OUTLIER

# Investigate that group
outlier_samples <- tech_reps$OGM108
ibs_matrix[outlier_samples, outlier_samples]
```

**Possible causes:**

1. **Sample swap:** One "replicate" is actually from a different colony
2. **Contamination:** Cross-sample contamination during extraction
3. **Poor quality:** One replicate has very low coverage/quality

**Solution:**

```{r fix-outlier, eval=FALSE}
# Remove the problematic replicate
tech_reps$OGM108 <- tech_reps$OGM108[1:3]  # drop the 4th one

# Re-run
result <- tree_trimmer(hc, tech_reps)
```

### Problem: Tree Never Cuts

**Symptom:** Even at the root of the tree, replicates don't unify.

```{r never-unified, eval=FALSE}
result <- tree_trimmer(hc, tech_reps)
# Warning: Group 'OGM024' never unified across all tree heights
```

**This means:** Your "technical replicates" are as divergent as unrelated samples.

**Solution:**

```{r verify-labels, eval=FALSE}
# 1. Verify sample names are correct
tech_reps$OGM024
hc$labels[grep("OGM024", hc$labels)]

# 2. Check if these are really technical reps
ibs_matrix["OGM024.1", "OGM024.2"]  # Should be >0.95

# 3. Check for possible mislabeling in your metadata
sample_metadata %>% filter(grepl("OGM024", sample))
```

### Problem: Buffer Choice Uncertainty

**Symptom:** You're not sure what buffer to use.

**Empirical approach:**

```{r buffer-sweep, eval=FALSE}
buffers <- seq(1.0, 1.3, by = 0.05)

results <- lapply(buffers, function(b) {
  result <- tree_trimmer(hc, tech_reps, buffer = b, verbose = FALSE)
  clone_groups <- cutree(hc, h = result$height)
  
  data.frame(
    buffer = b,
    height = result$height,
    n_clusters = length(unique(clone_groups)),
    largest_cluster = max(table(clone_groups))
  )
}) %>% bind_rows()

# Plot
plot(results$buffer, results$n_clusters, type = "b",
     xlab = "Buffer", ylab = "Number of clonal groups",
     main = "Effect of Buffer on Clone Detection")

# Look for the "elbow" - where increasing buffer stops
# drastically changing the number of groups
```

### Problem: Prefix Method Not Working

**Symptom:** `method = "prefix"` matches zero or wrong samples.

```{r debug-prefix, eval=FALSE}
# Your attempt:
result <- tree_trimmer(hc, c("OGM024", "OGM066"), 
                       method = "prefix", separator = ".")
# Warning: Prefix 'OGM024' matched zero samples

# Debug:
# 1. What are the actual labels?
head(hc$labels, 20)

# If they look like: "OGM024_1", "OGM024_2" (underscore, not period)
result <- tree_trimmer(hc, c("OGM024", "OGM066"),
                       method = "prefix", separator = "_")

# If they have extra prefixes: "Sample_OGM024.1"
# Use list method instead:
tech_reps <- list(
  OGM024 = grep("OGM024", hc$labels, value = TRUE),
  OGM066 = grep("OGM066", hc$labels, value = TRUE)
)
result <- tree_trimmer(hc, tech_reps, method = "list")
```

## Performance Optimization

For very large datasets (>10,000 samples):

```{r large-datasets, eval=FALSE}
# The bottleneck is cutree() called repeatedly
# Pre-compute all possible cuts:

system.time({
  # Standard approach
  result <- tree_trimmer(hc, tech_reps)
})

# For VERY large trees, consider:
# 1. Subsample for calibration
calibration_samples <- c(
  unlist(tech_reps),  # All tech reps
  sample(setdiff(hc$labels, unlist(tech_reps)), 500)  # Plus 500 random
)

hc_subset <- hclust(as.dist(dist_matrix[calibration_samples, calibration_samples]))
result <- tree_trimmer(hc_subset, tech_reps)

# Then apply to full tree
clone_groups_full <- cutree(hc_full, h = result$height)
```

## Exporting Results

### For Publications

```{r export-table, eval=FALSE}
# Create supplementary table
clone_table <- data.frame(
  Sample = rownames(ibs_matrix),
  Clonal_Group = clone_groups,
  Is_Technical_Rep = rownames(ibs_matrix) %in% unlist(tech_reps),
  Retained = rownames(ibs_matrix) %in% unique_genets$sample
)

write.csv(clone_table, "Supplementary_Table_Clones.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

### For Reproducibility

```{r save-results, eval=FALSE}
# Save the full result object
saveRDS(result, "clone_detection_result.rds")

# Save session info
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), "sessionInfo.txt")

# Save the exact code
writeLines(c(
  "# Clone detection parameters",
  paste("Buffer:", result$buffer),
  paste("Method:", "prefix"),
  paste("Separator:", "."),
  paste("Cut height:", result$height),
  "",
  "# Technical replicates used:",
  paste(names(tech_reps), ":", sapply(tech_reps, length), "replicates")
), "clone_detection_parameters.txt")
```

## Integration with Other Tools

### With pcangsd

```{r pcangsd-integration, eval=FALSE}
# After clone removal, re-run PCA
library(treeTrimmer)

# Clone detection
result <- tree_trimmer(hc, tech_reps)
clone_groups <- cutree(hc, h = result$height)

# Get clone-free samples
unique_genets <- metadata %>%
  group_by(cluster = clone_groups) %>%
  slice(1)

# Write BAM list for pcangsd
writeLines(unique_genets$bam, "samples_noclones.bams")
```

```{bash pcangsd-run, eval=FALSE}
# Run pcangsd with clone-free dataset
pcangsd -b genotypes_noclones.beagle.gz \
        -o pca_noclones \
        -t 8
```

### With NGSadmix

Similar workflow - just use the clone-free BAM list.

## When NOT to Use This Package

`treeTrimmer` is designed for a specific use case. Don't use it if:

1. **You don't have technical replicates** - The calibration requires known clones
2. **Your replicates aren't true clones** - If they're full siblings or parent-offspring pairs, this approach fails
3. **You have very few replicates** - Ideally, have at least 3 replicate groups with 2-3 members each
4. **Your data is phased haplotypes** - Use identity-by-descent (IBD) methods instead

## Getting Help

If you encounter issues:

1. Check the [GitHub issues page](https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/treeTrimmer/issues)
2. Provide a reproducible example with `reprex::reprex()`
3. Include your `sessionInfo()` output
4. Describe what you expected vs. what you got

```{r get-help, eval=FALSE}
# Minimal reproducible example template
library(treeTrimmer)

# Simulate data
set.seed(123)
dist_mat <- dist(matrix(rnorm(100), nrow = 20))
hc <- hclust(dist_mat, method = "average")

# Your problem here
tech_reps <- list(...)
result <- tree_trimmer(hc, tech_reps)
# Error: ...

sessionInfo()
```
